paper_title: Spectral Editing of Activations for Large Language Model Alignment
caption: : Left: Accuracy of all methods on each group of bias type in BBQ. Right: results on BBQ's testing set. All methods are applied on LLaMA-2-Chat-7B. For accuracy (A%_{}), higher values are better; for unknown-answer response rate (U%_{}), bias score (BS%_{}) and stereotypical response rate (SR%_{}), lower is better. We use bold font for the best result in each column, and mark the methods that improve ICL. : significant improvements on ICL in A% by pair-wise t-test with p < 0.05.
model_annotation: The plot titled “TruthfulQA” illustrates how a metric labeled “MCI” varies with the number of in-context “#Demonstrations,” showing one varying method curve along with two horizontal reference baselines. The x-axis is labeled “#Demonstrations,” uses a linear scale, and spans from 0 to 2000 with labeled ticks at 0, 500, 1000, 1500, and 2000. The y-axis is labeled “MCI,” uses a linear scale, and shows labeled ticks at 37, 38, and 39 (with gridlines aligned to these values). Three lines are shown: (1) a dark navy solid line with circular markers labeled “Linear SAE,” which starts near about 37.1 MCI at 0 demonstrations, rises to roughly 37.5 by around 100 demonstrations and to about 38.0 by around 200 demonstrations, stays in a narrow band just above 38.0 through roughly 500–1500 demonstrations (with a point near ~38.3 around 1000 and a point near ~38.1 around 1500), and then increases to its highest visible value near about 39.6 at 2000 demonstrations; (2) a pink/magenta dash-dot horizontal line labeled “LLaMA-2-chat-7B,” positioned at approximately 37.0 MCI across the entire x-range; and (3) a light cyan dashed horizontal line labeled “ICD,” positioned just below 38.0 (approximately 37.9 MCI) across the entire x-range, with an in-plot annotation reading “ICD (Prompt version)” near this line.
